quests.instruction: Find the orange-and-black insect that flies thousands of kilometres each autumn to spend winter in warm forests.
quests.hint: No single traveller completes the whole round trip.
quests.explanation: Monarch butterflies fly from North America to warm forests in Mexico for the winter. It takes several generations to make the return trip north.
quests.funFact: The monarchs that return north in spring are the great-grandchildren of the ones that left.
quests.question: Monarch Butterfly

quests.instruction: Spot the ocean giant that swims from cold feeding grounds to warm seas each year to have its calf.
quests.hint: It feeds in cold water in summer and gives birth in warm water in winter.
quests.explanation: Humpback whales feed in cold polar waters and travel to warm seas to breed and give birth.
quests.funFact: A humpback whale can travel thousands of kilometres in one direction.
quests.question: Whale

quests.instruction: Which seabird flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year, on the longest migration of any animal?
quests.hint: It chases summer around the world.
quests.explanation: Arctic terns fly from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year, a trip of tens of thousands of kilometres.
quests.funFact: An Arctic tern sees more daylight in a year than any other animal on Earth.
quests.question: Arctic Tern

quests.instruction: Spot the small mammal that can let its body cool to almost freezing during its long winter sleep.
quests.hint: Its heartbeat and breathing slow right down to save energy.
quests.explanation: Some ground squirrels hibernate with their bodies cooled to near freezing. Their heartbeat and breathing slow dramatically.
quests.funFact: A hibernating ground squirrel may breathe only a few times a minute.
quests.question: Ground Squirrel

quests.instruction: In autumn, most bumblebees die. Which one survives winter hidden underground?
quests.hint: She starts a new nest in spring, all by herself.
quests.explanation: In autumn, only new bumblebee queens survive. They hide underground over winter, then start new nests in spring.
quests.funFact: A bumblebee queen can sleep underground for six months or more.
quests.question: Bumblebee

quests.instruction: Which pond reptile can spend the winter at the bottom of a frozen pond, barely moving?
quests.hint: It uses almost no oxygen while the ice is above it.
quests.explanation: Some pond turtles spend winter in mud at the bottom of ponds. Their bodies slow right down, and they use very little oxygen.
quests.funFact: Some painted turtles can survive months under ice with very little oxygen.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Which orange-furred ape is in danger as rainforests are cleared to make way for farms and plantations?
quests.hint: It lives in only two places in the world.
quests.explanation: Orangutans lose their homes when forests are cleared. Protecting rainforests helps protect them.
quests.funFact: Orangutans live only on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra.
quests.question: Orangutan

quests.instruction: Name the animal that has been hunted illegally for its horn, and now has rangers guarding it.
quests.hint: Rangers patrol day and night to keep it safe.
quests.explanation: Rhinos have been poached for their horns. Rangers and conservation groups now work to protect them.
quests.funFact: Rhino horn is made of keratin, the same material as your fingernails.
quests.question: Rhino

quests.instruction: Name the fish that are in trouble in many places because so many are caught, and they grow slowly and have few young.
quests.hint: It takes them a long time to recover.
quests.explanation: Many sharks are caught in huge numbers. Because they grow slowly and have few young, they recover slowly.
quests.funFact: Some sharks don't have babies until they're more than ten years old.
quests.question: Shark

quests.instruction: Which insect's numbers have fallen as wildflower meadows have disappeared?
quests.hint: Planting flowers can help it find food.
quests.explanation: Many bees have lost their homes and food as meadows disappear. Planting wildflowers gives them nectar and pollen.
quests.funFact: A single bee visits thousands of flowers a day.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Which animals can be an early warning sign of polluted water, because their thin skin absorbs whatever is in the water?
quests.hint: If it disappears, scientists check the water.
quests.explanation: Frogs have thin skin that absorbs chemicals from water, so a decline in frogs can be an early warning that something is wrong.
quests.funFact: Scientists often use frogs as living water-quality testers.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Which colourful reef animals lose their shelter and food when warm water makes coral turn white?
quests.hint: Their coral home bleaches and loses its food supply.
quests.explanation: When the water gets too warm, coral turns white and may die. Reef animals lose shelter and food.
quests.funFact: Coral can recover if the water cools down again.
quests.question: Tropical Fish

quests.instruction: Which huge bird almost vanished from the United States, but recovered after a harmful chemical was banned?
quests.hint: The chemical thinned its eggshells.
quests.explanation: Bald eagles declined because the pesticide DDT made their eggshells too thin. After the chemical was banned, their numbers recovered.
quests.funFact: Bald eagles were taken off the US endangered species list in 2007.
quests.question: Bald Eagle

quests.instruction: Which hunter was brought back to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 after it had been missing for around 70 years?
quests.hint: Its return changed how other animals used the park.
quests.explanation: Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in the 1990s. Their return changed how elk and other animals behave.
quests.funFact: Wolves were missing from Yellowstone for about 70 years.
quests.question: Wolf

quests.instruction: Which sea animal was nearly wiped out by the fur trade, but has recovered in many places with protection?
quests.hint: Its extremely thick fur was prized.
quests.explanation: Sea otters were hunted for their fur until they were almost gone. Protection has helped them recover in some places.
quests.funFact: A sea otter's fur is among the thickest of any animal.
quests.question: Otter

quests.instruction: Which black-and-white birds breed on sea ice, which is shrinking in some places?
quests.hint: Their nesting platform is made of frozen sea.
quests.explanation: Emperor penguins breed on sea ice. If the ice melts early or breaks up, the chicks can be in danger.
quests.funFact: Emperor penguins breed in the Antarctic winter.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: Whether a hatchling is a boy or a girl depends on how warm the sand of its nest is. Which sea animal hatches this way?
quests.hint: Warmer sand means more girls.
quests.explanation: In sea turtles, the temperature of the nest decides the sex of the hatchlings. Warmer sand produces more females.
quests.funFact: In some places, almost all of the young sea turtles hatching are girls because the sand is so warm.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Which small birds struggle if the caterpillars they feed their chicks on appear weeks earlier than usual?
quests.hint: The timing of spring and the timing of their chicks might not match.
quests.explanation: Many small birds time their nesting for when caterpillars are plentiful. If warm springs bring caterpillars earlier, the chicks may go hungry.
quests.funFact: Warm springs can shift the caterpillar season earlier than it used to be.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: In parts of Africa, farmers hang beehives around fields to keep which giants away from their crops?
quests.hint: They don't like the buzz of angry insects.
quests.explanation: Elephants avoid bees. Beehive fences protect farmers' crops, and the farmers can also sell honey.
quests.funFact: Elephants can make a special rumble that warns others about bees.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: In parts of Kenya, flashing lights around the cattle pens at night help protect which big cat from being harmed?
quests.hint: The lights make it think someone is awake.
quests.explanation: Flashing lights around livestock pens scare lions away. That protects the cattle, and it stops farmers from needing to harm the lions.
quests.funFact: The flashing lights are made to look like someone walking around with a torch.
quests.question: Lion

quests.instruction: Which night-flying travellers can be confused by bright city lights, so some cities dim their lights during migration?
quests.hint: Lights can pull it off course.
quests.explanation: Migrating birds can be drawn off course by bright lights. Some cities switch off lights in tall buildings during migration seasons.
quests.funFact: Many migrating birds fly at night, using the stars to find their way.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: Which spiky visitors can roam between gardens if people leave a small gap in the fence?
quests.hint: It can travel more than a kilometre in one night.
quests.explanation: A gap about the size of a CD case lets hedgehogs travel from garden to garden to find food and mates.
quests.funFact: Some neighbourhoods have made "hedgehog highways" by making gaps in fences.
quests.question: Hedgehog

quests.instruction: Which beneficial beetles spend winter tucked into leaf piles and hollow stems?
quests.hint: Not tidying everything away gives them a place to shelter.
quests.explanation: Ladybugs spend winter in sheltered spots like leaf piles and hollow stems. Leaving a corner of the garden a little untidy helps them.
quests.funFact: Ladybugs that spend winter together can gather in groups of hundreds.
quests.question: Ladybug

quests.instruction: Which fluttering visitors sip water and minerals from damp soil, and are helped by a shallow dish with pebbles?
quests.hint: They need a safe place to land and drink.
quests.explanation: Butterflies sip minerals and water from damp soil. A dish of wet sand and pebbles gives them a place to do this.
quests.funFact: This habit is called puddling.
quests.question: Butterfly

quests.instruction: Find the clever animals that can become pushy and unwell when visitors feed them human food.
quests.hint: They learn to expect food, and may steal it.
quests.explanation: Feeding wild monkeys makes them depend on people and lose their natural fear. Their diet is much healthier without human snacks.
quests.funFact: Monkeys that learn to expect food from visitors may grab bags and snacks.
quests.question: Monkey

quests.instruction: Name the animals that can be disturbed when too many boats crowd around them on a tour, so guides must keep a distance.
quests.hint: They can seem friendly, but crowds stress them.
quests.explanation: Dolphins can be disturbed when boats get too close. Keeping a respectful distance helps them feed, rest and care for their young.
quests.funFact: Dolphins can be stressed by boat noise because they rely on sound.
quests.question: Dolphin

quests.instruction: Which small shore birds nest right on beaches, so people give them space in spring?
quests.hint: Their eggs look just like the pebbles around them.
quests.explanation: Plovers lay their camouflaged eggs on open beaches. Keeping away from roped-off areas protects the eggs and chicks.
quests.funFact: Plover chicks can run within hours of hatching.
quests.question: Plover

quests.instruction: If this animal disappears from a stream, scientists may check whether the water has been polluted. Which animal?
quests.hint: It needs cool, clean water that has plenty of oxygen.
quests.explanation: Many fish need clean, cool, oxygen-rich water. When they disappear, it can be a sign that the water is polluted.
quests.funFact: Trout and salmon need especially clean, cold water.
quests.question: Fish

quests.instruction: Which animal needs both land and sea to survive, so protecting just one isn't enough?
quests.hint: It feeds in the water but rests and has pups on land.
quests.explanation: Seals hunt in the water but rest and raise their pups on land. Both places need protecting.
quests.funFact: A seal can sleep both in the water and on land.
quests.question: Seal

quests.instruction: If a rainforest is protected, which animal's home is saved, because it spends almost its whole life in the treetops?
quests.hint: It almost never touches the ground.
quests.explanation: Sloths spend nearly all their time in the rainforest canopy. If the trees are cut down, they lose their homes.
quests.funFact: A sloth's slow movement helps it stay hidden among the leaves.
quests.question: Sloth
